items.note: Defined value for 0-11 km geopotential altitude. Observed environmental lapse rates vary about 4-8 K/km with humidity and stability; independent of planetary rotation.
g / c_p with g = 9.80665 m/s2 and c_p = 1004.7 J/(kg K); applies directly because the island canon uses Earth gravity and air.

items.description: Typical diurnal range of near-surface air temperature (ocean: skin SST) by surface type, mid-latitudes
items.note: Representative ranges for a 24 h day; clouds reduce DTR by 25-50% (Dai et al. 1999). Open-ocean SST range from Kawai & Wada (2007), land surfaces from Geiger et al. (2009). A 36 h day lengthens heating and cooling and is expected to widen the land range; the model is compared on the energy-balance mechanism, not these numbers directly.

items.description: Fractional reduction of land DTR under overcast vs clear skies
Mean annual precipitation across the Southern Alps (New Zealand), a mountain range in mid-latitude westerlies
items.note: Main-divide peak from Henderson & Thompson (1999), who estimate 10-12 m/yr at the wettest ridge; the station values are 1981-2010 normals. Distances are approximate perpendicular distances from the divide. Windward:leeward-basin ratio is about 5-8; peak:leeward-basin ratio about 20-30.

items.description: Ratio of windward lowland to leeward basin annual precipitation for a high (>2 km) mountain barrier in westerlies
items.note: Southern Alps (~5); similar ratios across the Cascades and the southern Andes.

items.description: Seasonal (warmest minus coldest month) range of sea-surface temperature, open ocean at 40-45 degrees latitude
items.note: About 3-6 K in the Southern Ocean and around New Zealand; larger (8-15 K) only in western-boundary-current regions of the northern hemisphere, which the island does not have.

items.description: Period band of mid-latitude synoptic variability (passage interval of cyclones and anticyclones)
items.note: Band-pass 2.5-6 day variance defines the storm track. Compare via the Eady growth rate on Marr'Kena, whose 36 h rotation changes f.

items.description: Lifetime of extratropical cyclones in the storm tracks
items.note: Mean tracked-system lifetime is about 3-4 days (Simmonds & Keay 2000; Hoskins & Hodges 2002); a long tail exceeds a week.

items.description: Eastward translation speed of mid-latitude cyclones
